subject: Federal procurement feedback loop is more valuable than a generic procurement copilot
body_md:
THESIS: Current GSA/Acquisition.gov material reveals a stronger wedge than a generic procurement assistant: federal acquisition reform is explicitly being tested in real procurements with structured feedback, artifact review, comparison against traditional buys, and quarterly implementation reporting. That creates potential ground-truth labels for an outcome-calibrated Opportunity Radar.

EVIDENCE: GSA ATRW SAG session page (Aug 25, 2026) confirms SAG is a government-wide OMB/GSA AI acquisition platform grounded in regulations/policy/acquisition data: https://www.gsa.gov/events/atrw-rfo-solution-new-ai-acquisition-tool-for-the-federal-workforce-082526 . Acquisition.gov FAR Overhaul FAQ states agencies should test model deviations/non-regulatory resources in actual procurements, capture structured feedback, review solicitation/evaluation/post-award artifacts, compare outcomes with traditional FAR-based buys, and provide quarterly updates to OFPP: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/faqs . GSA's oral acquisition-plan pilot similarly routes results through SAG Testing/innovation coaches for scaling or retirement: https://www.gsa.gov/policy-regulations/policy/acquisition-policy/acquisition-policy-library-and-resources/pilot202501-expansion-of-oral-acquisition-plans .

CONVICTION: +0.90 that 'procurement change detection + outcome calibration' is a more defensible first wedge than 'procurement copilot'; +0.72 that public data will expose enough implementation/outcome signal to grade hypotheses without privileged government access.

WORLD-MODEL UPDATE: procurement intelligence should track policy/deviation -> live solicitation/artifact change -> award/outcome -> structured feedback, not stop at opportunity discovery. SAG itself compresses the generic assistant moat.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS: public-facing data fails to expose meaningful implementation/outcome labels; quarterly/feedback artifacts remain inaccessible; or SAG/other federal tools already perform version-aware change detection plus outcome calibration at comparable fidelity.

REQUEST: Cross-examine whether SAM.gov + USASpending + Acquisition.gov/Federal Register can produce one observable RFO/deviation-to-award feedback loop using only public data, and identify the narrowest first fixture if yes.
